title: noo-addon-resources/1: an add-on's declared runtime inputs (resources.json)
description: A file of the add-on's signed bundle, listed in the bundle lock like system.json. The CLI (noo-cli/src/addons/resources.rs) is the authority: this schema states the shape, and the rules a schema cannot state are listed in x-noo-rules. docs/development/addons.md, 'Declaring runtime inputs', explains each kind. A fixture that passes is tests/fixtures/addons/rhaddon/resources.json.

uid.description: The uid the add-on's services run as. Every mount directory (0700) and file (0400) is owned by it. 0 is refused.

env.description: Receives the directory's host path; the overlay bind-mounts it read-only at target.

target.description: The container path. Not /, /proc, /sys or /dev. A db url names files by this path.

optional.description: Skipped with a notice, not refused, when it cannot be produced at launch. Not allowed on db.

hostname.description: noo-<addon> or noo-<addon>-<suffix> (the add-on name with _ as -), at most 63.

var.description: Must start with the add-on's own prefix (<NAME>_, name upper-cased, - as _), never NOO_, COMPOSE_ or DOCKER_, and must not be a variable a core compose file reads.

x-noo-rules: Secret material is delivered as a file only: tls_leaf key, addon_key, shared_secret, db key, db passfile.
Names (resources, mounts), variables (across mounts and env deliveries) and file destinations are unique.
db parts and network db need the bundle to declare system.json; db is the runtime role only, each part at most once.
A db url names ca, cert, key and passfile, which must each be declared with a file delivery; when the url is delivered as a file, into the same mount.
addon_key needs the overlay's x-noo-addon block (key: NOO_SVC_KEY_*); noo addons enable mints the key.
shared_secret is 32 random bytes kept in the encrypted store as NOO_ADDON_SECRET_<ADDON>__<NAME>, minted by noo addons enable when absent, rotated only by noo addons rotate-secret <name> <resource>.
A required resource that cannot be produced at launch refuses the add-on (named, the rest of the stack starts); an optional one is skipped with a notice.
Core produces no identity or account file.
